quote.translation: He says that "what is capable of being cut or of walking is also capable of not walking or of not being cut", and that "the possible of being and the possible of not being are the same" (Aristoteles, De interpretatione, 12, 21b), and he goes on to say that "from the possible of being follows the contingent of being, and the latter can be converted with the former" (τῷ μὲν γὰρ δυνατὸν εἶναι τὸ ἐνδέχεσθαι εἶναι, καὶ τοῦτο ἐκείνῳ ἀντιστρέφει) (Ib., 13, 22a).

quote.translation: He also says: "Therefore the possible means, in one sense, as was just said, that whose being false is not necessary; in another sense it means the true (what is); and in another sense it means what is true and contingently is" (τὸ μὲν οὖν δυνατὸν ἕνα μὲν τρόπον, ὥσπερ εἴρηται, τὸ μὴ ἐξ ἀνάγκης ψεῦδος σημαίνει, ἕνα δὲ τὸ ἀληθὲς [εἶναι], ἕνα δὲ τὸ ἐνδεχόμενον ἀληθὲς εἶναι) (Aristoteles, Metaphysica, Δ 12, 1019b).

quote.translation: Possibility is here determined in three ways: (1) from the standpoint of necessity, as "what is not necessary"; (2) from the standpoint of actuality, as "what is"; and (3) from the standpoint of contingency, as "what contingently is".

quote.translation: The passage is extremely rich in implication, but we should note that it identifies the possible with the contingent.

quote.translation: Boethius assigned possibile to δυνατόν (the possible) and contingens to ἐνδεχόμενον (the contingent), yet he said that "being contingent and being possible mean one and the same thing, and there is no difference whatever between them" (contingens esse et possibile esse idem significat, nec quidquam discrepat).

If we insist, he added, on stating a difference, it is merely a formal one, namely that the negative form of the one has the word impossibile, whereas there is no word incontingens to serve as the negative form of the other (Boethius, De interpretatione, Ed.
